thread:
alex: Quick heads-up — ran a 2k-token perf run with continuous-batching on the gpu-pool and perfetto shows recurring micro-spikes that blow out tail latency. link: https://perfetto.redwood/dev/8a7f3c
cheng: can you attach the nsys capture? perfetto is useful but i want kernel timelines + OS threads
alex: uploaded nsys to s3: s3://redwood-traces/2042101110-nsys.qdrep
jordan: quick skim: spikes correspond to a ~2.1ms window where queue_time jumps and we see a ~0.9ms cudaMemcpy + a ~1.0–1.3ms cutlass_gemm_v2 kernel pile-up. Looks like dispatch jitter not raw compute cost
maria: i also see periodic KV cache maintenance events every ~45s in the timeline that align with a small pause in batching coalescing, could be prefetch/sweep thrash
alex: repro command i used:

```
nsys profile --output=2042101110 --trace=cuda,osrt,cupti --sample=none --stats=true --duration=120 python run_inference.py --model redwood-3b --max-tokens 2048 --batching=continuous
```
cheng: flamegraph (nsys UI) shows two kernels alternating: `cutlass_gemm_v2_fp16` and `cutlass_gemm_asm_fused`. The switch happens when active_threads_per_block changes due to seq_len distribution. If kernel-selection heuristics flip, we might get kernel cache warmup + extra kernel selection path cost
jordan: notable: when selection flips to asm_fused the kernel launch count spikes (many small launches) whereas the plain gemm path runs fewer larger launches. That increases overhead substantially for small batches
maria: question — are we honoring `kernel_preference_weight` and `queue_coalesce_ms` correctly? If coalesce window is too small and we have KV sweep interfering, lots of 1–2 request batches will force less-efficient kernel path
alex: i toggled `queue_coalesce_ms` from 3 -> 12 and saw fewer spikes in a short run. But end-to-end latency improved only marginally because memcpy jitter remains. I captured host trace — there are occasional CPU scheduling bursts at the moment of memcpy (maybe driver/UCX?)
cheng: can you try forcing kernel selection to prefer `cutlass_gemm_v2_fp16` for shapes >= 256x256, just to see if that stabilizes dispatch? Also try `kv_cache_prefetch=false` in the run to rule out the maintenance interaction
alex: will run both. quick patch diff i tested locally to force preference:

```
--- a/runtime/kernel_selector.cc
+++ b/runtime/kernel_selector.cc
@@
- if (score_asm > score_cutlass) return asm_kernel;
+ if (score_asm > score_cutlass && override_pref != PREFER_CUTLASS) return asm_kernel;
```
(messy, just for experiment)
maria: perf-bot flagged a regression from yesterday that might be related: `kernel_dispatch_jitter` alert triggered at 2042030000 on main@d2fa — the alert notes an uptick in small-launch overhead
perf-bot: Automated note: regression check complete — recent commits touching `scheduler.cc` and `kernel_selector.cc` between main@d2fa..main@a4e3 increased kernel selection branch counts by 18% in microbenchmarks (see CI artifact: https://ci.redwood/build/3141)
jordan: short-term mitigation: bump `min_batch_for_asm` to 8 to avoid asm path for tiny batches. Long-term: make kernel selection cost-aware — include launch overhead estimate and memcpy cost in score function
cheng: also consider adding a tiny hysteresis window when switching kernel variants: only switch if score delta > 15% for N consecutive batches. That will avoid flip-flopping with seq_len noise
alex: results from quick experiments:
- forced prefer_cutlass: 30% reduction in tail P99 on the micro run, but median same
- queue_coalesce_ms=12: reduced number of small-launch windows by ~2x
- kv_cache_prefetch=false: removed the 45s periodic pause and smoothed batching, but throughput dropped ~4% (expected)
maria: sounds like we have two coupled effects: (1) KV maintenance occasionally breaks coalescing, introducing small-batch windows; (2) kernel-selection flip causes higher launch overhead when batches are small. Both amplify tail latency
jordan: next steps:
1) short patch: increase min_batch threshold for asm path + add hysteresis
2) schedule an nsys run with `--trace=cuda,osrt,api` capturing both normal and kv-prefetch toggled
3) add a synthetic microbenchmark that simulates seq_len mixture and measures branch flip frequency
4) consider measuring host-to-device memcpy variance under current NIC/driver (file a support ticket if necessary)
cheng: i'll own the synthetic benchmark; alex can run the full nsys with kv toggles; jordan/maria can prototype the selector hysteresis patch
alex: ok i'll upload new captures to s3 and paste links here when done. thanks all :thumbsup:
cheng: also, drop a short perfetto URL of the new capture into the release notes so PMs can see latency impact
alex: will do, ending trace now and kicking off the next runs.
